sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Brocchinia reducta is a terrestrial carnivorous bromeliad of nutrient-poor wet savannas, bogs and tepuis of the Guiana Shield. Its upright rosette forms a water-holding tank; leaves are about 25–50 cm long and the flower stalk may reach about 60 cm.

sections.title: Prey and image
sections.text: A slippery wax surface and absorptive leaf structures help trap and digest insects, especially ants. The plate's central tank, ant inset and flower stalk are consistent with the species. No human food use was located.
